spec.title: Windows context parity for Claude Code

tasks.title: Put .frame/bin on Windows PATH and name what lives there
tasks.whatChanged: launchEnv.prependFrameBin lost its supportsWrappers gate, so .frame/bin now leads the PATH of every PTY Frame spawns on Windows too — the ';' separator the function already carried finally gets reached. Two siblings joined it: wrapperFamily(platform) answers 'posix' or 'cmd', and wrapperFileName(toolId, { platform, canPassPaths }) returns the filename a tool's wrapper takes here, or '' when it earns none.
tasks.whyChanged: The gate was a category error: supportsWrappers asks whether this platform gets a POSIX wrapper for every tool, and PATH ordering is a different question — a .frame/bin that happens to be empty is a harmless first entry. wrapperFileName takes canPassPaths rather than a hardcoded 'claude only' list because a file-taking prompt flag is precisely what lets a batch wrapper stay plain; canPassPaths defaults to false so Windows opts a tool in explicitly and Codex/Gemini keep today's behaviour by construction. Both new functions take platform as a parameter, so Windows behaviour is asserted from a Mac.

verification.detail: 533 tests pass, 0 fail (19 in test/launchEnv.test.js, 8 of them new)

tasks.title: Teach Claude's launch to pass paths instead of prose
tasks.whatChanged: Claude's injection record gained promptFileFlag: '--append-system-prompt-file'. prepareLaunchAssets now also returns preambleRel and settingsRel — the same two files as project-relative, forward-slash paths. A new exported pure inlineInjectionFlags(tool, assets, platform) composes the wrapper-less branch and getLaunchCommand delegates to it, dropping its own flags.push pair and the now-unused `declared` local.
tasks.whyChanged: The composed line is typed into the PTY, and the preamble is 9 lines with 6 backticks: cmd.exe submits at the first newline and PowerShell reads a backtick as an escape, so --settings — and with it the spec-hint hooks — is the first thing lost. Two paths make the line single-line and quote-free. The paths are relative because the PTY's cwd is the project, which sidesteps a space in the path and the backslash a POSIX shell would eat. The file flag is chosen only where !supportsWrappers(platform): it has no --help row of its own, so an older CLI rejects it outright, and the POSIX path that works today must not acquire that version dependency (C3).

verification.detail: 545 tests pass, 0 fail (12 new in test/aiToolLaunch.test.js)

tasks.title: Write the .frame/bin/<id>.cmd wrapper template
tasks.whatChanged: Added getCmdWrapperTemplate(toolCommand, options) to src/shared/frameTemplates.js. It generates plain batch that resolves the real CLI with `for /f … in ('where <tool>')` skipping any hit whose %%~dpI is %~dp0, exits 127 with a stderr message when nothing remains, passes through under FRAME_NO_WRAP and when promptFileFlag is already on the line, walks up from %CD% to the directory holding .frame\, and routes every branch to one `call "%FRAME_REAL%" %FRAME_FLAGS% %*` followed by a bare `exit /b`. It returns '' for a tool with no promptFileFlag. 15 string assertions landed in test/frameTemplates.test.js.
tasks.whyChanged: The already-composed check scans arguments one at a time in a :frame_scan_args subroutine using %~1 rather than searching the whole of %* with substring substitution — that is a deviation from the plan's wording, taken because %* expands during parsing and a user argument carrying & or | would be re-parsed as syntax; %~1 strips cmd's quotes and compares a value. Exit-code propagation is goto-shaped rather than %ERRORLEVEL%-shaped because cmd.exe expands variables when it parses a parenthesised block, so the variable never appears in the file at all. Nothing executes in the tests: cmd.exe is not on this machine, and the real verification is T10's protocol.
